verdict: NXP grew revenue 19% to $3.8B as automotive and industrial chips surged, and kept about $24 of every $100 as profit.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.note: Chips for cars — the biggest business, up 13% as software-defined vehicles need more NXP content.

segments.name: Industrial & IoT
segments.note: Chips for factories and connected devices — up 39%, the fastest-growing large segment.

segments.name: Mobile
segments.note: Chips for phones and mobile devices — down 4%.

segments.name: Comm. Infra. & Other
segments.note: Communications infrastructure and other — up 54%, helped by data-center demand.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the next chips — up from $575M a year ago.

opex.name: Sales, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling chips and running the company.

opex.name: Amortization
opex.note: Amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets — a non-cash cost from past deals.

opex.name: Other operating expense
opex.note: Other income (expense) of -$3M inside operating results.

otherDetail: Other is financial expense of $97M, plus a $4M loss from equity-accounted investees shown separately in the flow — net income is $899M in total, $884M attributable to stockholders.
footerNote: NXP is a Dutch foreign filer; in this environment its Q3 2026 results were filed on Form 8-K (Exhibit 99.1) on Oct 27, 2026, with a full GAAP income statement, not a 6-K. Figures are GAAP; non-GAAP EPS was $4.20.
oneTimers: Non-GAAP results exclude $114M of share-based compensation, $36M of purchase-price-accounting effects and other items — the gap between GAAP EPS of $3.48 and non-GAAP EPS of $4.20.
follow100Note: Kept as profit is total net income of $899M; $884M was attributable to NXP stockholders after $15M for non-controlling interests.

takeaways.title: Growth came back
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 19% to $3,786M, with Industrial & IoT up 39% and Communications Infrastructure up 54%.

takeaways.title: High gross margin
takeaways.text: GAAP gross margin was 57.8% — $2,189M of gross profit on $3,786M of revenue.

takeaways.title: More buybacks authorised
takeaways.text: The board authorised a new $5B share repurchase program, on top of $1.3B remaining under the prior one.
